title: Keep a local value across calls
prompt: Issue sequential ticket numbers starting at 1. Keep the count across calls during one program run. No resets or concurrent calls are required; at most 1000 tickets are issued.
solution:
#include <iostream>

int nextTicket(){ static int count=0; return ++count; }

tests.label: Second ticket
tests.hint: A regular local variable starts over each call.

tests.label: Third ticket
tests.hint: The saved count should keep increasing.

tests.label: Fourth ticket
tests.hint: The state should still be present.

hints: A static local is initialized once and lives for the rest of the process.
The static keyword belongs on the counter declaration, not the return value.
explanation: The function controls the counter. Its local name is hidden from callers while the stored value lasts between calls; this is single-threaded.
